Issue: 576
Summary: OpENer v2.3 / master branch up to commit 76b95cf has a remotely reachable server-side memory corruption issue in the unconnected explicit-message SendRRData path. In GetAttributeList(), the response-space estimation for each returned attribute entry is 4 bytes too small because it counts the attribute value length but omits the fixed per-entry metadata that is later written: Attribute ID (2 bytes), status (1 byte), and reserved (1 byte). A valid GetAttributeList request against Identity instance 1 that repeatedly requests attribute 1 corrupts outer response metadata during response assembly; when the request also includes valid optional sockaddr info items 0x8000 and 0x8001, AssembleLinearMessage() continues encoding those CPF items and eventually crashes in AddIntToMessage() with a corrupted current_message_position.
Reproduce: Save the provided Python 3 PoC as `poc.py` and run it against an affected OpENer target on TCP port 44818, for example: `python3 poc.py 192.168.153.128 80 1 1`. The script connects to the target, sends `RegisterSession` (0x0065), then sends `SendRRData` (0x006F) containing a Null Address Item, an Unconnected Data Item with a CIP `GetAttributeList` request for Identity instance 1, `count=80`, and attribute ID `1` repeated 80 times, plus both optional sockaddr info items (`both_items=1`): type 0x8000 with AF_INET/port 0x2222/IP 192.168.153.200 and type 0x8001 with AF_INET/port 0x2223/IP 192.168.153.201. The script prints the session ID and then either a received response or `response=timeout`. [SOURCE id=issue:582:582-summary:a17fd2adbb9f kind=issue issue=582 path=distilled_issue/4.OpENer/#582.txt]
Issue: 582
Summary: OpENer 2.3.0 (commit 76b95cf) has an out-of-bounds read in CIP message parsing when handling malformed explicit requests with a forged EPath size. An ENIP SendRRData request can carry a very short CIP payload whose attacker-controlled path_size claims more path words than are actually available; because the parser continues decoding path segments without a remaining-length boundary, it reads past the end of the stack receive buffer. The report states this is remotely triggerable via network traffic and does not require authentication.
Reproduce: Use the provided Python 3 PoC against a target listening on 127.0.0.1:44818 by default (defaults: attempts=1, timeout=1.5, interval_ms=0, path_words=240, buffer_size=512). The client opens a TCP connection, sends ENIP RegisterSession (0x0065) with payload <HH>(1,0), and extracts the returned session ID. It then sends ENIP SendRRData (0x006F) for that session with 6 zero command-specific bytes plus a CPF whose item count is 3, containing a Null Address item (0x0000, length 0) and an Unconnected Data item (0x00B2) whose declared data length is only 2 bytes: service 0x0E followed by a forged path_size byte set to the requested path_words value. The PoC then appends repeated 0x20 0x01 bytes after that declared payload until the whole packet reaches 512 bytes, sends it, and waits for a reply. Reported outcomes are either RESP - response_len=... or FAIL - no response (reset, crash, or ASan abort), or an exception.
[/SOURCE]

[SOURCE id=issue:577:577-summary:f41c11d4b1b8 kind=issue issue=577 path=distilled_issue/4.OpENer/#577.txt]
Issue: 577
Summary: OpENer v2.3 / master branch up to commit 76b95cf is reported vulnerable in the TCP explicit-messaging path (RegisterSession -> SendRRData). A crafted EtherNet/IP SendRRData request can reach the Connection Manager instance services ForwardClose (0x4E), GetConnectionData (0x56), or SearchConnectionData (0x57) and trigger a stack-buffer-overflow read. The report attributes this to missing minimum request-body length validation in these handlers after Message Router path decoding: a long but syntactically acceptable padded EPath can consume the remaining CIP payload, leave request_data_size == 0, and the handlers still call GetUintFromMessage() / GetUdintFromMessage() on message_router_request->data. The reported result is an out-of-bounds read past the stack receive buffer, with stated impact of at least remote unauthenticated denial of service.
Reproduce: Prerequisite: an affected OpENer target on TCP port 44818; the report says no ForwardOpen or special build options are required. Use the provided Python 3 PoC (host argument or OPENER_HOST, default 127.0.0.1). It opens a TCP connection, sends RegisterSession (encapsulation 0x0065) to obtain a session handle, then sends SendRRData (0x006F) with CPF item count 2, a null address item, and unconnected-data item 0x00B2 carrying a CIP request for one target service: forwardclose=0x4E, getconn=0x56, or searchconn=0x57. [SOURCE id=issue:572:572-summary:4cac5b77f97f kind=issue issue=572 path=distilled_issue/4.OpENer/#572.txt]
Issue: 572
Summary: In OpENer v2.3 / master up to commit 76b95cf, the real TCP explicit-message path on port 44818 (`RegisterSession` / `SendRRData`) can reach `SetAttributeList()` with a default-registered, non-settable `kCipShortString` attribute: Identity class, instance 1, attribute 7 (`product_name`). For non-settable attributes, `SetAttributeList()` still advances over the attacker-supplied value, and for variable-length types it calls `GetCipDataTypeLength(attribute->type, message_router_request->data)` without validating remaining length. For `kCipShortString`, that leads to an unchecked 1-byte read via `GetSintFromMessage()`. With a long padded EPath positioning `message_router_request->data` at the end of the 512-byte stack receive buffer, ASan reports a stack-buffer-overflow / out-of-bounds read. The document states this is at minimum a remote unauthenticated denial of service in the default build.
Reproduce: Use OpENer v2.3 / master up to commit 76b95cf with the default Ethernet buffer size (`PC_OPENER_ETHERNET_BUFFER_SIZE=512`). Start the server, then run the provided Python 3 PoC in `crash` mode against TCP port 44818 (default host `127.0.0.1`, override with `OPENER_HOST`). The script first sends `RegisterSession`, then `SendRRData` carrying a CIP `SetAttributeList` request to Identity class 1, instance 1, attribute 7. In crash mode it builds a long padded EPath (`build_path(233)`) and sends `attr_count=1`, `attr=7`, with no short-string length byte following the attribute id. Expected result: ASan reports a stack-buffer-overflow / out-of-bounds read when `SetAttributeList()` skips the non-settable short string value.
[/SOURCE]

[SOURCE id=issue:593:593-summary:2b6de868ce19 kind=issue issue=593 path=distilled_issue/4.OpENer/#593.txt]
Issue: 593
Summary: OpENer decodes a CIP EPATH (electronic path) by reading a path_size count byte from the request and then
walking that many path words — without a remaining-buffer-length argument or bound. A request whose EPATH
path_size is larger than the actual data walks off the end of the incoming_message receive buffer.
Reproduce: Faithful ASan model (poc/opener_epath_oob_read_repro.c): a 300-byte redzoned buffer models the tail of
incoming_message; buf[0] = 255 (path_size = max), segment type bytes drive the 2-bytes/iteration walk with
no end check. ASan (poc/OPENER-01-asan.txt): heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1 past the 300-byte region.
[/SOURCE]
